extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, administrative-law researchers, agency managers, and statisticians tracking federal agency adjudicatory caseloads and dispositions
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction/interpretation of tabular federal-agency caseload data (backlog, age, manner of disposition, and time-to-disposition) across many types of administrative proceedings (FY1958). The page is a multi-table dataset classifying proceedings by agency/statute and reporting counts in standard buckets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlog and volume data fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 fields: Number of cases pending July 1, 1957; New cases commenced during fiscal year 1958; Cases reopened during the year; Cases closed during fiscal year 1958; Balance pending on June 30, 1958.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary volume metrics used across agencies in Table 1. Each row lists a type of proceeding (by agency/statute) and the counts for the five columns above. Example entries: 'Number of cases pending July 1, 1957', 'New cases commenced during fiscal year 1958', 'Cases closed during fiscal year 1958'. Footnotes indicate some agencies report estimated figures for proceedings awaiting action (see CAB note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proceedings (agency + statutory classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are classified by agency and statute (e.g., 'FEDERAL POWER COMMISSION — NGA §4(e) investig., 15 USC §717c(e)'; 'SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION — Stop orders (SA), 15 USC §77h(d)'; many others across 21 agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each row/topic identifies a specific proceeding type by name and statutory citation; this classification is the primary dimension for grouping counts. Use these labels to filter or aggregate by agency or statutory proceeding. The page lists many specific proceeding names and corresponding U.S. Code citations (useful for legal or programmatic mapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-of-proceedings buckets
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 2 age buckets: 'pending 6 months or less'; 'over 6 months but not over 12'; 'over 1 year but not over 2'; 'over 2 years but not over 3'; 'pending over 3 years'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 reports, for each proceeding type, the total pending June 30, 1958 and the counts falling into each age bucket above. Use these buckets to analyze latency/aging. Note: age data are not available for some large subsets (e.g., 14,355 Social Security cases and 1,681 Indian probate cases), per footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner-of-disposition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 3 disposition categories: 'Dismissal or withdrawal without decision on the merits'; 'Examiner decision which became final without review'; 'Agency decision on the merits without examiner decision'; 'Agency decision on the merits after examiner decision'; 'Default, consent, settlement, compromise and other'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3 breaks closed cases down by these disposition manners for each proceeding type. Footnotes explain subtypes (e.g., consent dismissal, consent order, moot/default counts) and occasional agency-specific notation (e.g., 'terminated as a medical review case and re-instituted in complaint status'). Use these categories to study outcomes and how often cases end without a merits decision vs. with examiner/agency decisions or settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall time-to-disposition buckets
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 4 time-to-disposition buckets used for proceedings closed during the fiscal year: 'Closed in 6 months or less'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Over 1 year but not over 2'; 'Over 2 years but not over 3'; 'Over 3 years'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 applies these buckets to analyze elapsed time from commencement of proceeding to final agency disposition. The table is organized by agency and proceeding type and often filtered to particular final-decision categories (for example, 'FINAL DECISION ON THE MERITS AFTER AN EXAMINER'S DECISION'). Use these buckets to measure speed of resolution. Examples: counts for 'Certifs. of conven. & nec.' show distribution across these time intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-decision subtype: 'Final decision on the merits after an examiner's decision'
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific final-decision subtype reported in Table 4: cases closed by a final agency decision on the merits occurring after an examiner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 presents time-to-disposition buckets specifically for this outcome. It is a distinct analysis slice (not all closed cases) and allows assessment of how long matters that proceed through examiner hearings and then receive an agency final decision take to resolve. Other final-decision slices may exist implicitly (e.g., cases decided without examiner involvement) but this slice is explicitly tabulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLRB case-type coding and mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: National Labor Relations Board case codes and descriptions: CA cases (alleged §8(a) unfair practices by employer), CB cases (alleged §§8(b)1,2,3,5,6 unfair union practice), CC cases (alleged §§8(b)(4)(A),(B),(C) union practice), CD cases (alleged §8(b)(4)(D) unfair union practice), RC cases (pet. for cert. of representatives), and combinations (e.g., CA-CB, CA-CC, CA-CD, CA-RC, CA-RD including decertification petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table rows use these short codes to label NLRB case types and report counts/age/disposition. The mapping to statutory citations (29 USC §§159,160 etc.) is provided and should be used when interpreting NLRB rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand totals and partial-coverage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables report 'TOTALS' per agency and a 'GRAND TOTALS - 21 AGENCIES' (e.g., 'The last column of Table 1 reports 23,541 proceedings of all types pending on June 30, 1958').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that grand totals may include proceedings for which age or other detailed data are not available; the text explicitly notes that age data appear for only a subset (7,505) of the 23,541 proceedings. When aggregating, respect footnoted exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data caveats and footnotes affecting interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes and explanatory notes: (1) 'Except for safety enforcement proceedings, all of the data reported by the CAB include actual figures for cases in process, but estimated figures for cases awaiting action.' (2) 'FCC data for Part A are not broken down as to types of proceeding, but are consolidated so that the totals are available.' (3) 'Of the 14,355 Social Security cases pending on June 30, 1958, a total of 5,060 had been pending before examiners more than 60 days... average time from assignment to an examiner was 6 or 7 months.' (4) 'All of these cases were suspended ... during required reconsiderations ... under successive remands.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notes affect data quality and coverage: some counts are estimates, some agencies consolidate types, and some large programmatic suspensions distort time measures. Incorporate footnote caveats into any analysis or comparisons; do not treat all table cells as equally precise.
